note: TTS input for docs/video_narration.md. Numbers are spelled out. [word](/phonemes/) fixes words missing from the Kokoro (misaki) dictionary: Jetson, Orin, Nebius, Nemotron, int. Scene 5b is held until the positive-control result.

scenes.1: Same robot. Same task. One run succeeds, one fails. Before I ship this policy to a tiny [Jetson](/dʒˈɛtsən/), how do I know which model I can trust?
scenes.2: This is an S O one oh one arm running an A C T policy on a [Jetson](/dʒˈɛtsən/) [Orin](/ˈɔɹɪn/) Nano Super. We taught it with one hundred and twenty teleoperated demonstrations, and trained it on [Nebius](/nˈɛbiəs/). From that one policy, we built twenty-six candidate engines with TensorRT: full precision, half precision, and twenty-four [int](/ˈɪnt/) eight builds that differ only in how they were calibrated. QuantGate scores every candidate offline first, then checks the arm. Every real trial is blinded. The operator never knows which engine is running, and the results stay sealed until all the trials are logged. That way, no candidate gets picked after we have seen how it did.
scenes.3: QuantGate puts three things side by side for every candidate: what it costs on the real device, how it scored offline, and what it did on the real arm. Training and the offline audit ran on [Nebius](/nˈɛbiəs/) Jobs. The engines run as TensorRT on the [Jetson](/dʒˈɛtsən/).
scenes.4: Measuring changed the decision. On this [Jetson](/dʒˈɛtsən/), half precision was the cheapest engine, not [int](/ˈɪnt/) eight, and on the arm it went nineteen for twenty. The audit's top picks did no better than random picks: seventy-three out of seventy-five, both ways. What really moved success was grip, and position.
scenes.5: The A I layers get checked too. In our setup, Cosmos Reason, served on a [Nebius](/nˈɛbiəs/) endpoint, called this frame a success. It missed all seven failures. [Nemotron](/nˈimOtɹˌɑn/) Super on Token Factory writes the deployment report, and every number in it is checked against the evidence.
scenes.6: What you take away is a review, not a guess. Half precision is the cost-favored candidate. Its placement matched full precision, but the success comparison still needs more trials. The weak spots are grip, and start position. And the review tells you exactly what to test next.
